findings.title: Embedded post author link uses inverted lightness values
findings.body: The light-theme branch was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `70%`, while the dark-theme branch uses `$secondary` at `30%`. This is the inverse of the required dark-theme mapping (30% on primary should become 70% on secondary) and also changes the established light-theme color. Embedded-post author links will become overly faint in light themes and too dark/low-contrast in dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message counter reverses its intended lightness mapping
findings.body: This rule previously used `$primary` at 70% but now uses `$primary` at 30% and `$secondary` at 70%. The light-theme appearance is therefore changed unexpectedly, and the dark-theme value is the opposite of the complementary mapping used elsewhere (`primary 70%` should map to `secondary 30%`). The message-length counter can be substantially less legible than before, particularly in dark themes.

findings.title: Topic-map heading loses its intended high-contrast lightness
findings.body: The `.topic-map h3` light-theme value was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to 50%, rather than preserving 20% and adding the complementary dark-theme value `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)`. This changes the heading color in light themes and makes the dark-theme heading much dimmer than the corresponding desktop topic-map heading.

findings.title: Group member names no longer preserve the original light-theme color
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `$primary` at 30%, but this change replaces it with a 50%/50% pair. The correct dark-theme counterpart for the existing 30% primary value is 70% secondary. This both alters the light-theme hierarchy between member names and titles and gives dark themes a weaker/inconsistent name color.

findings.title: Mobile group member names use the wrong dark-theme counterpart
findings.body: The mobile `.group-member-info .name` rule has the same regression as desktop: the previous 30% primary value was replaced by 50% primary / 50% secondary. It should retain 30% for light themes and use 70% secondary for dark themes, otherwise mobile member names lose their intended visual hierarchy and do not match desktop.

findings.title: Category-list notification text remains unadapted for dark themes
findings.body: ` .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` directly. In a dark color scheme this continues to derive the muted text color from the foreground `$primary` rather than `$secondary`, which is the issue this change set is intended to address. It should use `dark-light-choose(...$primary..., ...$secondary...)` like the other topic-list text rules.
